questions.q: What is the actual fix applied to northfield-redshift-copy-role?
options: Add a new s3:ListBucket statement on the bucket ARN, alongside the existing s3:GetObject statement
Remove the s3:GetObject statement entirely
Delete the role and create a brand-new one from scratch
Grant the role full S3 administrator access
questions.explain: The fix is additive: the missing s3:ListBucket statement is added alongside the existing, still-correct s3:GetObject statement.

questions.q: Why is s3:ListBucket's Resource value the bucket ARN with no object path, while s3:GetObject's Resource ends in /orders/*?
options: ListBucket is a bucket-level operation that only makes sense against the bucket itself, while GetObject reads individual object keys
Both should actually use the exact same Resource value
This is a typo that happens to work by accident
Object-level ARNs are never valid for any S3 action
questions.explain: Enumerating what exists under a prefix is a bucket-level operation; reading an object's bytes is an object-level operation. Each needs its own resource scope.

questions.q: Why does s3:GetObject alone feel sufficient when creating the role, but isn't?
options: COPY must enumerate which Parquet part-files exist under the prefix before it can fetch any of them, and enumeration is gated by a different action entirely
GetObject actually already includes ListBucket's permissions automatically
Parquet files never need to be listed, only read
COPY reads files in a fixed, pre-known order that skips enumeration
questions.explain: Reading sounds like 'the job,' but COPY can't reach that step without first listing the prefix, which is a separate, bucket-level permission.

questions.q: How is the fix validated after being applied?
options: Re-run the Lesson 5 COPY manually, confirm no new sys_load_error_detail rows, then re-run the Lesson 6 row-count/sum pair against curated vs. fact_orders
Only check that the IAM console saved the policy without an error message
Delete analytics.fact_orders and assume it will repopulate correctly on its own
Only re-run the EventBridge rule and wait a full day to see if it silently worked
questions.explain: Validation re-runs the actual failing operation by hand and checks both the error table and an exact row-count/sum match against source.

questions.q: Why doesn't the Lesson 8 nightly scheduled refresh need its own separate fix?
options: EventBridge, the Glue trigger, and the Python Shell load job all ultimately call through the same IAM role, so fixing that role's policy once fixes every future scheduled run
The nightly schedule uses a completely different role that was unaffected
EventBridge rules re-check IAM permissions only once per calendar month
The nightly schedule was actually already working correctly all along
questions.explain: northfield-redshift-load re-issues the same COPY under the same role, so the single policy fix resolves every future run of the chain.
